subject: Demo recap + proposed POC activation cadence for Aurora Health
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@aurorahealth.ai>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv@aurorahealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-07-14T15:08:00-07:00
Subject: Demo recap + proposed POC activation cadence for Aurora Health

Hi Elena / Rajiv —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and a proposed POC activation cadence so we can lock next steps:

TL;DR: We propose a 6-week POC focused on (1) ingest and search accuracy (week 1–2), (2) workflow integration and latency tuning (week 3–4), and (3) acceptance & handoff (week 5–6). Owners and success criteria below. I attached a one-page POC outline and a short SLA summary.

What we demoed:
- Document ingestion and semantic search over clinical notes
- Streaming API latency at 8–12ms median for 512 token requests in our dedicated config
- Tooling for prompt-controlled hallucination checks and eval dashboards

Proposed POC activation cadence (high level):
1) Kickoff & data ingest (Week 0–1): onboarding, secure transfer, sample ingestion (owner: Aurora Eng + Redwood SE - Ben)
2) Evaluation sprint A (Week 1–2): accuracy & relevance tests on 5k queries, define baseline metrics (owner: Aurora PM - Rajiv; Redwood: Marissa)
3) Integration sprint (Week 3–4): integrate API endpoints into triage workflow, tune batching/quantization settings for cost/latency (owner: Aurora Eng; Redwood SE - Ben)
4) Acceptance & handoff (Week 5–6): success sign-off, playbook for production cutover, optional follow-up canary (owner: Aurora Ops + Redwood CSM - Logan)

Suggested success criteria (please confirm):
- Precision@5 >= 0.78 on clinician-labeled queries (evaluation set to be mutually agreed)
- Median API latency <= 20ms 95th percentile under expected test load (see baseline in attachment)
- False-positive hallucinations < 2% on critical-safety prompts (measured via eval harness)
- Integration end-to-end call < 250ms additional latency in staging flow

Logistics / security notes:
- We recommend SFTP or presigned S3 for sample data (we support customer-managed VPC if required).
- We'll provide a scoped service account and an audit log export for the POC period.

Attachments: POC-outline-AuroraHealth.pdf (one-pager), SLA-summary-Redwood-1p.docx

Next asks from Aurora: please confirm the success criteria above, whether the proposed 6-week cadence works, and your preferred kickoff week (we have window starting 2028-07-25).

Thanks — looking forward to locking dates.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Senior CSM, Redwood Inference
log an.wright@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

——

From: Elena Torres <elena@aurorahealth.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@aurorahealth.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-07-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo recap + proposed POC activation cadence for Aurora Health

Thanks Logan — helpful summary. A few quick clarifying questions from our side before we confirm:

1) Data transfer & scope: we prefer presigned S3 for the initial sample set. Can you confirm retention policy on Redwood's hosted POC environment (how long do you keep samples)?
2) Security: will we need Private deployment for this POC to satisfy our DLP rules, or can we run the POC on Redwood hosted with customer-managed encryption keys?
3) Success metric: the Precision@5 target looks reasonable; can we also add a qualitative clinical-signoff step (2 clinicians to approve) as an acceptance gate?
4) Timeline: the team is available for a kickoff week of 2028-07-25 but we need the initial data transfer details and a non-prod endpoint by EOD 2028-07-24. Is that doable?

Also, can you share a short summary of any SLA exceptions for POCs (uptime/response for test endpoints)? The SLA doc you attached felt production-focused.

If you can confirm answers to 1–4 we can lock the kickoff.

Best,
Elena Torres
Director of Data Products, Aurora Health
elena@aurorahealth.ai | +1 (617) 444-2222

——

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@aurorahealth.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv@aurorahealth.ai>
Date: 2028-07-16T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo recap + proposed POC activation cadence for Aurora Health

Elena — quick answers inline.

> 1) Data transfer & scope: we prefer presigned S3 for the initial sample set. Can you confirm retention policy on Redwood's hosted POC environment (how long do you keep samples)?
We keep inbound sample data for 30 days by default for POCs, then we automatically expire unless you request retention. If you need shorter retention we can set a 7-day auto-delete for the bucket. We can also disable persistence entirely and use streaming-only ingestion for the sample run.

> 2) Security: will we need Private deployment for this POC to satisfy our DLP rules, or can we run the POC on Redwood hosted with customer-managed encryption keys?
For most proofs we run on hosted with CMEK (customer-managed encryption keys) and VPC peering if needed. Private deployment is only required for fully air-gapped/regulatory constrained projects — based on our call it sounds like hosted + CMEK + audit logs should be fine. If you want, Redwood can spin up a dedicated VPC endpoint for the POC.

> 3) Success metric: the Precision@5 target looks reasonable; can we also add a qualitative clinical-signoff step (2 clinicians to approve) as an acceptance gate?
Absolutely — adding a clinical-signoff gate is straightforward. I'll add that to the acceptance checklist.

> 4) Timeline: the team is available for a kickoff week of 2028-07-25 but we need the initial data transfer details and a non-prod endpoint by EOD 2028-07-24. Is that doable?
We can provide presigned S3 instructions and a non-prod API endpoint by 2028-07-24 EOD PDT. To hit that timeline we need the sample dataset by 2028-07-22 EOD to run basic ingestion checks.

Attachment notes: the POC-outline contains the eval harness we will run; the SLA-summary is a short production-style doc, but for POC we operate with a best-effort test endpoint (99% uptime historically across POC runs). We can provide an interim uptime target in the DocuSign workflow if you want a formal acknowledgment for the trial period.

Next steps (Ben / Logan to action):
- Ben to send presigned S3 instructions + ingestion checklist (today)
- Marissa to share evaluation template and baseline query set format (tomorrow)
- Logan to draft kickoff invite + proposed agenda for week of 2028-07-25

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
